newsitem.title: KENYA: Aid workers ordered out of Zaire city - U.N..
newsitem.headline: Aid workers ordered out of Zaire city - U.N..

text.p: The United Nations ordered an evacuation of aid workers from the eastern Zairean city of Bukavu on Saturday because of increasing insecurity, a U.N. spokeswoman said.

"There are orders from the U.N. security office in New York to carry out a total or partial evacuation of staff from Bukavu to Entebbe airport in Uganda today," said Brenda Barton, a spokeswoman for the U.N. World Food Programme (WFP) in Nairobi.

"We have two Buffalo aircraft, one of which has already arrived in Entebbe from Nairobi and the other is on the way. They will go into Bukavu to pull our people out," she said. Each plane carries 42 passengers.
"Three WFP vehicles were stolen in Bukavu last (Friday) night by the Zairean army. Security is definitely worsening."
She said there were a total of 98 international staff in Bukavu. She said New York had left it open for aid officials on the ground to decide whether the evacuation was total or partial.
A plan to airlift food into Bukavu from Entebbe for some of the nearly 300,000 refugees displaced by more than a week of fighting was put on hold because of the evacuation, Barton said.
